--- Slide 4: The Firm’s Profits We assume that a firm’s ---
The Firm’s Profits We assume that a firm’s objective is to maximize profits. Profits – the total revenue received from selling the product minus the total costs of producing the product, or: Profits = total revenue – total costs 10/26/2026 4

--- Slide 5: Revenue and Cost Profits = total revenue – ---
Revenue and Cost Profits = total revenue – total costs Total Revenue = price of the product X quantity sold at that price = P .Q Total Cost – The sum of the fixed costs and the variable costs of production.  This includes all costs such as salaries, rent, material costs, business permits, etc.  In economics, the total costs should also include all opportunity costs. --- Slide 7: A Price Competitive Market Competitive market – A ---
A Price Competitive Market Competitive market – A market in which no firm has power to influence the market price of a good. Example – edible oil, sugar or commodity market Price-taker – Any firm that takes the market price as given;  firm cannot affect the market price Because firms in competitive markets are price takers, we can derive the supply curve of each firm by asking how much each firm is willing to supply at a given price. 10/26/2026 7

--- Slide 8: Production Decisions of a Firm Production Technology Describe ---
Production Decisions of a Firm Production Technology Describe how inputs can be transformed into outputs Inputs: land, labor, capital and raw materials Outputs: cars, desks, books, icecream, sugar, etc. Firms can produce different amounts of outputs using different combinations of inputs 10/26/2026 8
[Notes: 15]

--- Slide 9: Production Decisions of a Firm Cost Constraints Firms ---
Production Decisions of a Firm Cost Constraints Firms must consider prices of labor, capital and other inputs Firms want to minimize total production costs partly determined by input prices Firms must be concerned about costs of production 10/26/2026 9

--- Slide 10: Production Decisions of a Firm Input Choices Given ---
Production Decisions of a Firm Input Choices Given input prices and production technology, the firm must choose how much of each input to use in producing output Given prices of different inputs, the firm may choose different combinations of inputs to minimize costs If labor is cheap, firm may choose to produce with more labor and less capital 10/26/2026 10

--- Slide 11: Production Decisions of a Firm For a given ---
Production Decisions of a Firm For a given level of output, profit maximization is same as cost minimization. If a firm is a cost minimizer, we can also study How total costs of production vary with output? How the firm chooses the quantity to maximize its profits? We can represent the firm’s production technology in the form of a production function 10/26/2026 11

--- Slide 12: The Technology of Production Production Function: Indicates the ---
The Technology of Production Production Function: Indicates the highest output ( q ) that a firm can produce for every specified combination of inputs For simplicity, we will consider only labor (L) and capital (K) Shows what is technically feasible when the firm operates efficiently Let us begin with one variable input 10/26/2026 12

--- Slide 13: Short Run vs Long Run Short-Run – A ---
Short Run vs Long Run Short-Run – A time period where at least one input is fixed, and other inputs are allowed to vary.  In our analyses, we usually allow the labor input to vary, and capital input to stay fixed in the short-run. Long-Run – A time period long enough for all inputs (both capital and labor) to vary. 10/26/2026 13

--- Slide 1: MBA 801: Product Strategy & Go-To-Market Execution Instructor: ---
MBA 801: Product Strategy & Go-To-Market Execution Instructor: Prof. Elena Vance | Stanford Graduate School of Business Course Module: Strategic Product Management & SaaS Economics Core Objective: Understand how modern tech products build defensible moats and scale through user-driven loops.

--- Slide 2: The Strategic Hierarchy: Vision, Mission, Strategy & Roadmap ---
The Strategic Hierarchy: Vision, Mission, Strategy & Roadmap Product Vision: The long-term aspirational future state the company seeks to create (e.g., Google: Organize the world's information). Product Mission: What the company delivers today, for whom, and how customer value is created. Product Strategy: The coherent set of integrated choices defining where we play and how we win against competitors. Product Roadmap: The prioritized sequence of user problems to solve and milestones scheduled over time.

--- Slide 3: Defining Product-Market Fit (PMF) & The Sean Ellis ---
Defining Product-Market Fit (PMF) & The Sean Ellis Rule PMF Definition: The inflection point where customer retention flattens into a healthy plateau and organic word-of-mouth powers compound growth. The Sean Ellis 40% Benchmark: Ask active users: 'How would you feel if you could no longer use this product?' If >= 40% reply 'Very disappointed', the product has achieved sustainable product-market fit. Premature Scaling Risk: Aggressive spending on customer acquisition before reaching the 40% threshold destroys enterprise capital.

--- Slide 4: Go-To-Market (GTM) Motions: PLG vs Sales-Led Growth Product-Led ---
Go-To-Market (GTM) Motions: PLG vs Sales-Led Growth Product-Led Growth (PLG): Uses the product itself to drive acquisition, conversion, and expansion (e.g., Slack, Figma, Notion). Key PLG Metrics: Time-to-Value (TTV), Natural Frequency of Use, Product Qualified Leads (PQLs). Sales-Led Growth (SLG): Relies on enterprise SDRs, multi-stage demos, and executive relationship selling (e.g., Salesforce, Workday). Hybrid Motion: Start with bottom-up PLG adoption, then overlay enterprise sales to capture 6-figure enterprise agreements.

--- Slide 5: SaaS Unit Economics & The Golden Metric Formulas ---
SaaS Unit Economics & The Golden Metric Formulas Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) = Total Sales & Marketing Expenses / Number of New Customers Acquired. Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) = (ARPU * Gross Margin %) / Churn Rate. The Golden Ratio: LTV:CAC must be >= 3.0x for sustainable venture-scale growth. CAC Payback Period = CAC / (Monthly ARPU * Gross Margin %). Top-quartile SaaS companies recover CAC in < 12 months.

--- Slide 6: Prioritization Frameworks: RICE vs Kano Model RICE Framework ---
Prioritization Frameworks: RICE vs Kano Model RICE Framework Formula: RICE Score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort. - Reach: Number of target users impacted per quarter. - Impact: 0.25 (minimal), 0.5 (low), 1.0 (medium), 2.0 (high), 3.0 (massive). - Confidence: 100% (high data), 80% (medium), 50% (low hunch). - Effort: Measured in person-months of engineering and design. Kano Model Categorization: Must-haves (basic stakes), Performance attributes (linear satisfaction), Delighters (innovative excitement).

--- Slide 7: Case Study: Figma Disruptive Collaborative Canvas Technology Wedge: ---
Case Study: Figma Disruptive Collaborative Canvas Technology Wedge: WebGL and browser-based WebAssembly eliminated heavy desktop software installation. Multiplayer Network Effect: Real-time collaborative design turned single designers into internal company champions. Monetization Flywheel: Free tier for individual contributors; team workspace paid tier unlocked enterprise design systems. Result: 150%+ Net Dollar Retention (NDR) leading to massive market share capture from legacy desktop suites.

levels.title: Active Recall vs. Passive Reading
levels.explanation: Passive rereading produces a dangerous false hallucination of competence. Active recall forces the neural wetware to reconstruct knowledge without external references, triggering synaptic plasticity.
levels.analogy: Rereading notes is like watching someone else play an arcade fighter. Active recall is putting your quarters in and executing the 10-hit combo yourself.
levels.product_example: Duolingo refuses to show static vocab tables. It immediately forces users into a live translation fight, strengthening memory retrieval pathways.

levels.title: Spaced Repetition & The Forgetting Curve
levels.explanation: Ebbinghaus demonstrated memory decays exponentially without active reinforcement (~70% lost in 48 hours). Reviewing at calculated intervals resets the decay curve and consolidates memory into permanent storage.
levels.analogy: Cramming is like overclocking a graphics card until it melts. Spaced repetition is balanced liquid cooling that runs peak performance 24/7.
levels.product_example: Anki and SuperMemo use mathematical decay algorithms (SM-2) to ping you with a card at the exact millisecond before total memory erasure.

levels.title: The Feynman Model & Mental Schemas
levels.explanation: Richard Feynman proved true mastery requires explaining concepts in jargon-free language that a 10-year-old grasps. Buzzwords are smoke bombs used by imposters to hide architectural knowledge voids.
levels.analogy: If you can’t build a drone with raw components, reciting the parts catalog doesn’t make you an aerospace engineer.
levels.product_example: Steve Jobs stripped away technical specs: not a "5GB spinning mechanical drive", but "1,000 songs in your pocket".

levels.title: Cognitive Load & Dual Coding
levels.explanation: Human working memory is bottlenecked at 4 to 7 discrete chunks. Splitting information into simultaneous visual and verbal channels doubles transmission capacity without frying the user’s cognitive circuit.
levels.analogy: Your working memory is a 512MB RAM stick. If you load 4K video textures with zero compression, the system crashes. Clean visual schemas are your GPU.
levels.product_example: Figma and Miro dominate because spatial diagrams let engineering teams comprehend sprawling microservice architecture without mental paralysis.

questions.question: Which action triggers maximum synaptic reinforcement during a study sprint?
options: Highlighting sentences in fluorescent pink marker
Answering practice exam prompts with notes closed
Listening to an audiobook while driving
questions.correct_answer: Answering practice exam prompts with notes closed
questions.explanation: Retrieval practice under desirable difficulty strengthens memory traces far more than passive rereading.

questions.question: True or False: The feeling of fluency when rereading your own notes is a proven guarantee of exam mastery.
questions.explanation: Fluency heuristic tricks students into mistaking recognition for actual recall capability.

questions.question: The cognitive blindspot where students mistake visual familiarity for true mastery is the illusion of ______.
questions.explanation: The illusion of competence happens when looking at notes makes material feel easy, but you cannot reproduce it without looking.

questions.question: MISSION: Your startup team must internalize a complex API integration before demo day tomorrow. What is the highest ROI study tactic?
options: Have engineers conduct closed-book whiteboarding sprints where they recreate the API flow from memory
Distribute a 50-page PDF and ask everyone to read it before midnight
Record a 4-hour meeting and tell them to watch it at 2x speed
Memorize code snippets without understanding data contracts
questions.correct_answer: Have engineers conduct closed-book whiteboarding sprints where they recreate the API flow from memory
questions.explanation: Active retrieval on a whiteboard exposes false assumptions and cements architectural comprehension.

questions.question: What is the neurological mechanism activated when you struggle to retrieve an answer?
questions.explanation: Desirable difficulty stimulates neural pathways to physically re-wire for faster future access.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of new lecture material is lost within 48 hours without spaced review?
questions.explanation: The Ebbinghaus Forgetting Curve shows dramatic drop-off (~70%) in the initial 48 hours without reinforcement.

questions.question: True or False: Cramming for 8 hours before an exam yields higher 6-month retention than 1 hour daily for 8 days.
questions.explanation: Cramming only impacts volatile working memory. Long-term consolidation requires sleep and spaced intervals.

questions.question: The algorithm widely used in computer-aided spaced repetition flashcard engines is ______-2.
questions.explanation: SuperMemo-2 (SM-2) calculates intervals and ease factors.

questions.question: TACTICAL CASE: You are rolling out a new product onboarding flow for users. To prevent churn drop-off, how do you schedule tooltips?
options: Dump all 24 feature tooltips in the user’s face in the first 60 seconds
Trigger contextual, micro-onboarding prompts spaced across Day 1, Day 3, and Day 7 based on user actions
Provide no onboarding and email a 30-page user manual after signup
Lock the app until they watch a 45-minute video tutorial
questions.correct_answer: Trigger contextual, micro-onboarding prompts spaced across Day 1, Day 3, and Day 7 based on user actions
questions.explanation: Spaced, action-triggered learning respects working memory limits and embeds habit loops.

questions.question: What is the optimal moment to review an item in a spaced repetition cycle?
options: Right before you are about to forget it
questions.correct_answer: Right before you are about to forget it
questions.explanation: Retrieving an item right at the edge of decay causes the strongest consolidation impulse.

questions.question: What is the core test of the Feynman Model?
options: Explaining the concept to a 10-year-old using simple words and concrete analogies
Using at least 5 technical acronyms per sentence
Creating a 3D animated video with no audio
questions.correct_answer: Explaining the concept to a 10-year-old using simple words and concrete analogies
questions.explanation: If you cannot communicate it simply without jargon crutches, your own comprehension has gaps.

questions.question: A compressed framework or representation of how something works in the real world is known as a mental ______.
questions.explanation: Mental models allow product managers to reason from first principles.

questions.question: EXECUTIVE BRIEFING: You need to convince the CFO to fund an AI caching layer. Which explanation wins the budget?
options: "It operates as an LRU Redis key-value cluster with distributed hash rings over Kubernetes pods."
"Think of it like a barista keeping the 5 most popular drinks ready on the counter, so lines move 80% faster and customers spend $400K more."
"Trust the engineering team because Redis is popular on GitHub."
"Here are 20 pages of server latency logs for your weekend reading."
questions.correct_answer: "Think of it like a barista keeping the 5 most popular drinks ready on the counter, so lines move 80% faster and customers spend $400K more."
questions.explanation: The barista analogy connects technical architecture to business speed and revenue outcomes.

questions.question: True or False: Using high-density jargon in product presentations proves superior competence to executive leadership.
questions.explanation: Jargon obscures real mechanics and indicates a lack of conceptual translation ability.

questions.question: When practicing the Feynman Model and your explanation hits a dead-end, what is step 3?
options: Return to the source lecture slides to patch that exact concept gap
Invent an answer and hope nobody notices
questions.correct_answer: Return to the source lecture slides to patch that exact concept gap
questions.explanation: The Feynman Model is a diagnostic loop designed to pinpoint and repair knowledge leaks.

questions.question: What is the typical working memory capacity limit of human consciousness?
questions.explanation: George Miller and modern cognitive psychology confirm working memory bottleneck at 4-7 chunks.

questions.question: True or False: According to Dual Coding Theory, combining visual diagrams with verbal narrative improves retention compared to text alone.
questions.explanation: Dual coding leverages parallel cognitive processing channels, creating two independent retrieval pathways.

questions.question: In Cognitive Load Theory, unnecessary mental friction created by bad UI layout is called ______ cognitive load.
questions.explanation: Extraneous cognitive load wastes mental bandwidth on decoding chaotic presentation rather than learning.

questions.question: UI OPTIMIZATION: Your analytics show 55% of users abandon your signup form. How do you apply Cognitive Load Theory to fix it?
options: Display all 32 inputs on one massive scrolling page with bright red asterisks
Break the flow into 3 progressive, chunked steps with visual milestone markers
Add 4 animated promotional banners next to the credit card input
Hide the submit button until the user scrolls past legal disclaimers
questions.correct_answer: Break the flow into 3 progressive, chunked steps with visual milestone markers
questions.explanation: Chunking information reduces extraneous load and matches human working memory thresholds.

questions.question: Which type of cognitive load is beneficial because it directly constructs mental schemas and deep mastery?
questions.explanation: Germane load is the productive mental effort dedicated to processing and integrating knowledge.

questions.question: BOSS ENCOUNTER ROUND 1: The Scope Creep attacks with a 40-feature wishlist right before sprint freeze! What is your weapon of defense?
options: Ruthless RICE prioritization anchored in verified user retention metrics, rejecting non-core items
Say yes to all 40 features and ask engineers to work 90-hour weeks
Quietly delete the backlog and pretend the email was lost in spam
questions.correct_answer: Ruthless RICE prioritization anchored in verified user retention metrics, rejecting non-core items
questions.explanation: CRITICAL HIT! Rigorous prioritization anchored in retention metrics damages the Scope Creep monster.

questions.question: BOSS ENCOUNTER ROUND 2: The Scope Creep tries to distract the team with a 50-slide text-heavy architecture deck. How do you counter?
options: Apply Dual Coding: transform the spec into clean visual interaction flows with chunked responsibilities
Print out the 50 slides on poster board and paste them on the wall
Ignore architecture entirely and start writing frontend CSS
Schedule a 6-hour meeting to read the slides word-for-word
questions.correct_answer: Apply Dual Coding: transform the spec into clean visual interaction flows with chunked responsibilities
questions.explanation: CRITICAL HIT! Dual coding reduces extraneous cognitive load and aligns the engineering team.

questions.question: BOSS ENCOUNTER ROUND 3: True or False: Agreeing to customer feature requests without validating underlying root pain points is sound product management.
questions.explanation: CRITICAL HIT! Building what users say they want without uncovering the underlying job-to-be-done breeds monstrous bloat.

questions.question: BOSS FINAL STRIKE: The Scope Creep is at 25% HP! It demands to know: what is the single most definitive indicator of real Product-Market Fit?
options: Sean Ellis 40% benchmark: over 40% of surveyed users would be "very disappointed" if the product disappeared tomorrow
Total number of Twitter retweets on the launch announcement
The aesthetic quality of the landing page gradient
How many venture capital firms sent connection requests on LinkedIn
questions.correct_answer: Sean Ellis 40% benchmark: over 40% of surveyed users would be "very disappointed" if the product disappeared tomorrow
questions.explanation: FINISHING BLOW! The Sean Ellis PMF benchmark measures true user reliance and retention.
